* [x] CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. Minor bug fixes and documentation changes should not be included.

items.title: Note in the upgrade guide that PostgreSQL 18.4+ fixture loading acquires more locks
items.body: This adds a section to "Upgrading from Rails 8.1 to Rails 8.2" for a change on main that breaks existing apps and that the guide doesn't mention yet. Loading fixtures on PostgreSQL 18.4+ acquires more locks (#57378), so parallel test workers loading fixtures into databases with a few hundred foreign keys can fail with `out of shared memory`, as they did when I ran an app's test suite on main.

items.title: Let a temporary SQLite table or view hide a permanent one in the schema readers
items.body:
The batched SQLite schema readers from #58498 join each pragma to a list of `sqlite_master` and `sqlite_temp_master` rows. While fixing their table-name case lookup, I found that when a temporary table has the same name as a permanent one, both rows match, and the pragmas resolve both to the temporary table, as SQLite does. So columns and indexes are duplicated, and the primary key becomes composite.

The list now takes a permanent table or view only when no temporary table or view has its name, which is how SQLite resolves identically spelled names. Collations and check constraints now come from the temporary table's CREATE statement too; 8-1-stable read the columns from the temporary table but the statement of the permanent one.

Shared index names remain a separate issue.

items.title: Don't freeze serialized column defaults
items.body:
#59083 [freezes a model's default attributes](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/9e82904f18daceb77761a5705dde0c529026cea2/activerecord/lib/active_record/model_schema/schema_context.rb#L137-L139) when [every one is freezable](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/9e82904f18daceb77761a5705dde0c529026cea2/activemodel/lib/active_model/attribute.rb#L42-L44), and new records copy the cast value. For a serialized attribute the coder decides that value, and it may not round-trip the column default. OpenProject's [`HealthReport`](https://github.com/opf/openproject/blob/9ae6b5cc50ba3b675661f751d2ca9f361cb1f0b3/app/models/health_report.rb#L33) loads its [`t.jsonb :results, null: false, default: {}`](https://github.com/opf/openproject/blob/9ae6b5cc50ba3b675661f751d2ca9f361cb1f0b3/db/migrate/20260428133700_create_health_reports.rb#L34) as `[]`, so in its test suite on Rails main, `HealthReport.new(subject: storage).save!` raises `PG::NotNullViolation` (8.1: only after a read).

Now serialized types don't let their defaults be frozen, and encrypted types ask the type they encrypt. Models with a serialized attribute keep 8.1's writable defaults; other models, including those with JSON, array and hstore defaults, stay frozen.

items.title: Allow registering parameter parsers in place during boot
items.body:
Since #57952, the default parameter parsers are [the frozen `DEFAULT_PARSERS` constant](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/bdb3d960121e7eb73a61c04099d1eef3c821e397/actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/http/parameters.rb#L31), and [assigned parsers are frozen too](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/bdb3d960121e7eb73a61c04099d1eef3c821e397/actionpack/lib/action_dispatch/http/parameters.rb#L45). Running OpenProject's test suite on Rails main, I found that registering a parser in place now raises `FrozenError` while the app boots:

```ruby
ActionDispatch::Request.parameter_parsers[:jsonapi] = ->(raw) { JSON.parse(raw) }
# 8.1: registered; main: FrozenError: can't modify frozen Hash
```

Released gems do this from their railtie or engine: [graphiti 2.2.3](https://github.com/graphiti-api/graphiti/blob/1b11959b323cce2d9d8185a9f6c18164c9763eb1/lib/graphiti/rails/railtie.rb#L84), [graphiti-rails 0.4.2](https://github.com/graphiti-api/graphiti-rails/blob/f8031d1f9659825d7a41f73a4650c616085c187c/lib/graphiti/rails/railtie.rb#L75), [jsonapi-rails 0.4.1](https://github.com/jsonapi-rb/jsonapi-rails/blob/75314ad9742e8fe4746e1c8418779d2aacf7d9b8/lib/jsonapi/rails/railtie.rb#L43) and [scimitar 2.15.0](https://github.com/pond/scimitar/blob/a7edc24d208ef4d2316c982c48bd2a5fe4fdcb5d/lib/scimitar/engine.rb#L14), which OpenProject uses, so apps using them don't boot on main.

This restores in-place registration, keeping parsers mutable until `ractorize!`, which then freezes them on every class that includes `ActionDispatch::Http::Parameters`. Parsers assigned or included after that are frozen as before, and `DEFAULT_PARSERS` itself stays frozen. Reading them from another Ractor still requires every parser value to be shareable.

items.title: Restore ActiveModel::SecurePassword::MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH_ALLOWED
items.body:
This keeps `ActiveModel::SecurePassword::MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH_ALLOWED` as a public constant that points at `BCryptPassword::MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH_ALLOWED`. Comparing the public API of 8-1-stable and main, I found that #56041 moved the constant into the new `BCryptPassword` class when it added `algorithm:`. The removal is unreleased.

Applications and gems use the old name to cap password length, so on main they raise `NameError` when the code loads:

```ruby
# Spree 6.0.2, spree/core/lib/spree/core/configuration.rb
preference :maximum_password_length, :integer, default: ActiveModel::SecurePassword::MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH_ALLOWED, env: 'SPREE_MAXIMUM_PASSWORD_LENGTH'

# open-build-service, src/api/app/models/user.rb
validates :password, length: { minimum: 6, maximum: ActiveModel::SecurePassword::MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH_ALLOWED }, allow_nil: true
```

Sources: [Spree 6.0.2](https://github.com/spree/spree/blob/439f7350926011abc4a986e7e8373299fb405e68/spree/core/lib/spree/core/configuration.rb#L187), [open-build-service master](https://github.com/openSUSE/open-build-service/blob/2881e368ac2b42a01945455593698b3f99b4af16/src/api/app/models/user.rb#L122).

The constant preserves the BCrypt byte limit and is defined directly on `SecurePassword` again, as in 8.1. Loading stays as lazy as on main: `SecurePassword` already requires `bcrypt_password.rb`, and the bcrypt gem is still only required when a password is hashed. The new test fails without the constant.

items.title: Keep the UTC offset in Time#change for times with a zone object
items.body:
On a `Time` whose zone is an object (`TZInfo::Timezone` or `ActiveSupport::TimeZone`), `change` couldn't always stay in the hour that repeats when clocks go back. TZInfo zones raised `TZInfo::AmbiguousTime`, also from Active Model's datetime cast when it truncates precision. `ActiveSupport::TimeZone` could jump to the other occurrence of that hour.

`change` now tries the time's own UTC offset first and keeps it when the zone agrees. Otherwise the zone decides, as before.

At 00:30 UTC on 2026-10-25, both zones are in the first of two identical local hours:

| Zone | Start | `change(sec: 1)` on main | With this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Berlin, `TZInfo::Timezone` | 02:30:00 +0200 | raises `AmbiguousTime` | 02:30:01 +0200 |
| Dublin, `ActiveSupport::TimeZone` | 01:30:00 +0100 | 01:30:01 +0000, an hour later | 01:30:01 +0100 |

Still unchanged: a time in the skipped spring hour raises `PeriodNotFound`, and with a TZInfo zone an ambiguous time raises when neither occurrence has the original offset.

items.title: Declare Prism dependencies in Action View and Railties
items.body:
Ruby master, targeting 4.1, turns prism from a default gem into a bundled gem (ruby/ruby@a1efb9ae6b, [ruby-lang #22379](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/22379)), so under Bundler `require "prism"` only works when prism is in the bundle. #56631 removed the Ripper fallbacks because Ruby 3.3 ships prism as a default gem, so Action View and Railties now require prism without declaring it.

Most apps get prism indirectly today, since irb >= 1.17, minitest 6, rdoc 8 and rubocop-ast depend on it. An app whose lockfile has none of them, for example one with an older irb locked, gets a `LoadError` on Ruby master from `ActionView.eager_load!` and Ruby-based dependency tracking, and from the test runner and `bin/rails notes` when they run. Released 8.1 still has the Ripper fallback and isn't affected.

This declares `prism` in both gemspecs, since each requires it directly. It is unversioned, as Active Support does for `base64`, `drb`, `bigdecimal` and `json`, so the default gem on Ruby 3.3 to 4.0 keeps satisfying it. `Template#spot` keeps its `Ruby::Prism` handling.

items.title: Deprecate a positional table name in Arel::Table.new
items.body:
`Arel::Table.new(:users)`, which Rails 8.1 and earlier accept, raises `ArgumentError` on main, because #57829 made the table name the `name:` keyword. Arel is nodoc, but gems and apps call it: flipper 1.4.2 fails in `Flipper::Adapters::ActiveRecord#get_all`, and so do Discourse and Docuseal; the comments on #57829 report Intercom and GitHub.

As suggested in #57829, a positional name, as in `Arel::Table.new(:users)` or `Arel::Table.new(nil, klass: User)`, now keeps working with a deprecation warning and behaves exactly as `name:`. A call passing both uses the positional name; neither the Rails 8.1 signature nor main's allows both. `as:`, `klass:` and `type_caster:` were already keywords, so nothing else changes.

items.title: Build the association alias tracker only for through chains
items.body:
`AssociationScope#scope` builds an `AliasTracker` for every association scope, and for a direct `belongs_to` or `has_many` throws it away unused: `get_chain` only uses the tracker for the reflections after the first. Building it isn't free, because `Relation#alias_tracker` looks up the model's connection pool and checks a connection out and back in to read `table_alias_length`. This runs for every association reader that builds its scope and for every association relation (`post.comments.where(...)`).

`get_chain` now takes the relation and builds the tracker when it reaches the second reflection, with the same arguments as before. A direct association no longer touches the connection while building its scope; the query that runs it still does.

| Callgrind instructions per call on Ruby 4.0.7, interpreter / YJIT | main | this PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `post.author` | 692k / 298k | 647k / 282k (−6.5% / −5.3%) |
| `post.comments.to_a` | 873k / 359k | 828k / 343k (−5.2% / −4.6%) |
| `post.comments.where(body: "c").to_a` | 1,049k / 430k | 1,004k / 417k (−4.3% / −2.9%) |

On ruby-bench, shipit runs 2.6% fewer instructions per iteration in the interpreter and 1.8% fewer with YJIT. Each direct association scope allocates 2 fewer objects; 36 of 56 workloads in six apps allocate fewer objects in the interpreter, and 42 with YJIT.

items.title: Inline connection_pool dependency
items.body:
I want to decrease the dependency surface of Active Support and this one is a very easy one to remove.

We are inlining the dependency into the framework, respecting the LICENSE.

After the deprecated redis adapter is removed, only the memcache store will rely on this connection pool and we can decide whether to keep it or not.

items.title: Match Rack::BadRequest errors in ActionDispatch::ParamError
items.body:
### Motivation / Background

`ActionDispatch::Request#POST` converts `ActionDispatch::ParamError` into `ActionController::BadRequest`, but `ParamError.===` only matched three explicit Rack error classes (`ParameterTypeError`, `InvalidParameterError`, `ParamsTooDeepError`). Other malformed-body errors that Rack ≥ 3.1 tags with the `Rack::BadRequest` marker module, such as `Rack::Multipart::BoundaryTooLongError` or `Rack::Multipart::MultipartPartLimitError`, escaped as 500s instead of 400s.

We hit this in production: a `PUT`/`PATCH` `multipart/form-data` request with a boundary longer than 70 characters raises `BoundaryTooLongError` at the first `params` access in the controller. `ExceptionWrapper.rescue_responses` has no entry for it, so the client gets a 500 for what is a malformed request.

### Detail

`ParamError.===` now also matches `Rack::BadRequest` when it is defined. The explicit classes are kept because Rails still supports Rack 3.0, which predates the marker module.

### Additional information

Two tests in `test/dispatch/request_test.rb` (boundary too long on `PUT`, `multipart_file_limit` exceeded), only defined on Rack >= 3.1, where `Rack::BadRequest` exists. Both fail on `main` and pass with this change. `test/dispatch/request*`, `debug_exceptions_test` and `show_exceptions_test`: 298 runs, 0 failures.

Companion Rack change so that `Rack::MethodOverride` stops letting the same errors escape on `POST`: https://github.com/rack/rack/pull/2505.

### Checklist

- [x] This PR is a fix
- [x] Tests are included
- [x] CHANGELOG entry added (actionpack)

items.title: Locate Action Text attachables in bulk
items.body:
### Summary

Rendering Action Text content resolves every attachment's SGID with its own query, and an attachment in a gallery is resolved three times. Saving is quadratic: each attachment's `record` presence validation calls `RichText#blank?`, which renders the whole body, and every render resolves every attachment again.

Blob lookups for a message with 20 image attachments, 10 of them in a gallery, in the Action Text test app:

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Render | 40 | 1 |
| Create | 420 | 2 |
| Update | 20 | 1 |

Preloading is not a workaround: `with_rich_text_body_and_embeds` loads the Active Storage associations, but rendering still resolves each SGID one at a time.

Fixes #36177.

### Approach

`ActionText::Attachable.from_attachable_sgids` is the bulk counterpart to `from_attachable_sgid`, returning `{ sgid => attachable }` through `GlobalID::Locator.locate_many`, one query per model class. Signature verification, custom locators and STI base-class SGIDs behave as before.

`ActionText::Content` memoises the result, hands it to its attachment galleries, and carries it into the content that `render_attachments` returns, so the gallery pass reuses it. Anything that cannot be located in bulk falls back to the existing `Attachable.from_node` chain, so missing, remote and content attachments are unchanged.

### Tests

Query counts for N attachments, for a gallery across rendering, memoisation across renders, and ordering when some attachables cannot be located.

Found in production on [Pagecord](https://pagecord.com), which now runs an equivalent patch. Against a copy of an image-heavy blog, a page of 15 posts went from 372 queries to 30.
